gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.sentence: We must ___ our efforts to finish on time (STRONG).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: strengthen. A base verb follows 'must'.

gaps.sentence: He ___ denied knowing anything about the plan (FIRM).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'denied': firmly. Note the doubled m before -ly.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: He ___ forgets to bring the tickets, as usual (TYPICAL).
gaps.hint: adverb of frequency needed to modify 'forgets' (-ly)
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'forgets': typically means in the usual way.

gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: The crisis could ___ the economic situation (WORSE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: worsen means to make worse. A base verb follows 'could'.

gaps.sentence: The medicine is available without a ___ (PRESCRIBE).
